prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
This 2010 manifesto sets out policies across the economy, public services, welfare, security, the environment, constitutional reform and foreign affairs.

Economy and finance
- Support the recovery before tightening from 2011–12; plan to more than halve the deficit by 2014 via growth, targeted tax rises and lower‑priority cuts, while protecting frontline spending on childcare, schools, the NHS and policing.
- Savings: major efficiency drives, reduced overheads and consultancy, a 1% cap on basic public‑sector pay uplifts in 2011–13, public‑sector pension reforms, and asset sales.
- Tax: maintain new top rate on very high earners, reduce pension tax relief for the best off, introduce a bonus tax and a 1p rise in National Insurance (with protections for low earners).
- Financial reform: higher bank capital, “living wills,” a global levy, tougher remuneration oversight, more competition, and realising stakes in publicly controlled banks while securing taxpayer value.
- Growth and industry: UK Finance for Growth (£4bn), a Green Investment Bank, high‑speed rail, universal broadband, strengthened corporate governance (two‑thirds shareholder support for takeovers), and support for SMEs (rate relief holiday, credit adjudicator, Time to Pay).

Jobs, welfare and housing
- Job guarantees: funded jobs/training for young people at six months (mandatory by ten), and a guaranteed job after two years’ unemployment.
- Make work pay: minimum wage to rise at least with average earnings; a “Better Off in Work” guarantee (£40/week).
- Skills: expand advanced apprenticeships and Skills Accounts.
- Housing: stamp duty holiday for first‑time buyers up to £250k (two years), paid for by a higher rate on £1m+ homes; expand affordable and council housing; stronger mortgage regulation; private landlord register; target to end rough sleeping by 2012.

Consumer finance
- Transform the Post Office into a “People’s Bank”; universal right to a basic bank account; levy to expand affordable credit; clamp down on high‑cost lenders; portable bank/ISA numbers; a single consumer‑finance regulator.

Education
- Increase frontline spending on Sure Start, childcare, schools and 16–19 learning; expand free nursery hours and places for two‑year‑olds.
- Guarantees: one‑to‑one/small‑group tuition for pupils falling behind; personal tutors in secondary; parental triggers for leadership change; more accredited school groups.
- Raise participation to 18; expand advanced apprenticeships; widen university access while sustaining quality; review HE funding.

Health and care
- Protect NHS spending; up to £20bn efficiencies reinvested in care.
- Guarantees: 18‑week treatment (or funded private alternative), cancer tests within one week of referral, routine health checks for ages 40–74, choice of qualified provider, extended GP access, and wider access to psychological therapies.
- More care at home, personal care plans and budgets; tougher cleanliness and safety standards.
- National Care Service in stages: free home care for greatest needs (from 2011), cap residential care costs after two years (from 2014), and a pathway to a comprehensive, free service post‑2015.

Policing, justice and immigration
- Maintain police and PCSO numbers; neighbourhood policing with performance report cards and interventions in failing areas.
- Faster action on anti‑social behaviour with a right to seek injunctions; expand Community Payback.
- Use of CCTV and DNA within set limits; more prison capacity; enhanced victims’ services and virtual courts.
- Borders and migration: points‑based system, stronger enforcement, English language testing pre‑arrival, and tighter links between status and entitlements.

Culture, communities and digital
- Deliver the 2012 Olympics legacy; widen sport in schools; enable supporter trusts in football; keep free museum entry; protect post offices and viable pubs; support social enterprise and mutuals; uphold public service broadcasting; universal broadband.

Environment and rural affairs
- Target around 40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020; 400,000 green jobs by 2015; expand renewables, nuclear and CCS; reform planning and regulation to unlock £150bn investment.
- Home energy “Pay As You Save,” smart meters, landlord insulation standards; move toward zero waste and restrict landfill; expand protected habitats, maintain Green Belt, increase woodland; supermarket ombudsman; strengthen rural services and broadband.

Constitution and governance
- Referendums on the Alternative Vote and an elected second chamber; fixed‑term parliaments; explore a written constitution.
- Clean‑up measures: independent expenses regime, lobbyist register, controls on MPs’ outside roles, and recall for serious misconduct.
- Devolve more power and data transparency; strengthen city‑regions and local scrutiny.

Defence, security and international
- Strategic Defence Review; maintain the nuclear deterrent; modernise forces; enhanced support for service personnel and veterans.
- Afghanistan strategy focused on protecting the population, training local forces and transition.
- Active role in EU and global reform; meet 0.7% aid by 2013 in law; drive progress on the Millennium Development Goals and climate cooperation.
